Amazon to invest $7 billion in renewable energy in India by 2030
Amazon also announced four new wind and solar projects in India, including its largest wind farm contracted in Asia to date.
Share
Written by 
Charles Clark
Published:

November 17, 2026
4 min read
Key takeaways
Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030.
Amazon's existing India projects will power the equivalent of more than 3.5 million homes.
Amazon's new global goal aims to cut the carbon intensity of its electricity by 65% by 2030.
Amazon has announced plans to invest $7 billion in renewable energy projects in 
India
 by 2030, significantly expanding its renewable energy portfolio and supporting the country’s transition toward a more sustainable and resilient energy future.
This is in addition to $4 billion that Amazon already contracted in renewable energy investments in the country, making Amazon one of India’s leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy.
Amazon continues to be one of the world’s leading corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy
With more than 700 projects globally, Amazon is investing in over 40 gigawatts of carbon-free energy, which is enough to power more than 12.1 million U.S. homes.
Amazon also announced four new utility-scale wind and solar projects with a combined total capacity of 934 megawatts (MW). They include a 234 MW wind farm in Karnataka, Amazon’s largest wind project contracted in Asia to date; a 200 MW combined solar and wind project also in Karnataka; a 300 MW solar project in Madhya Pradesh; and a 200 MW solar project in Rajasthan.
The projects are secured through power purchase agreements, long-term contracts in which a company agrees to buy electricity from a specific wind or solar project. They’re part of Amazon’s existing $4 billion in contracted projects in India and, once operational, will have a combined capacity of more than 2 gigawatts (GW)—enough to generate electricity equivalent to the annual needs of more than 3.5 million Indian households.
Amazon’s new goal to reduce carbon intensity
Amazon’s renewable energy investments in India will contribute to the company’s new global goal to reduce the carbon intensity of the electricity powering its operations by 65% by 2030.
The new target means that every unit of electricity the company consumes will be associated with 65% fewer carbon emissions compared to a 2019 baseline. Against the backdrop of growing global energy demand, the target represents a milestone on the way to Amazon’s 
Climate Pledge
 goal to be net-zero carbon by 2040.
Amazon announces it will invest $48 billion in India by 2030
Since launching in India, Amazon has digitized 12 million small businesses and supported 2.8 million jobs. 
“Our renewable energy investments in India reflect years of sustained effort, planning, and collaboration across the industry. This additional investment of $7 billion underlines our long-term commitment, helping bring additional wind and solar capacity online while contributing to India’s energy security and long-term renewable energy ambitions,” said Kara Hurst, Amazon’s chief sustainability officer.
“By expanding access to renewable energy at scale, we aim to help meet India’s growing electricity demand, strengthen the country’s energy security, and contribute to its ambitious goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.”
How Amazon is scaling carbon-free energy in India
Amazon’s renewable energy portfolio in India includes 14 utility-scale wind and solar projects that add carbon-free energy to the grid, as well as 43 on-site solar installations across its facilities in India that help power its operations. Together, these 57 projects reflect a sustained focus on scaling carbon-free energy across its operations and supporting the development of renewable energy capacity at scale.
Investments in new carbon-free energy projects add new sources of carbon-free energy to the grid that powers homes, hospitals, schools, and businesses, while also supporting Amazon’s operational needs. They support the modernization of energy infrastructure, help maintain stable and affordable electricity access over time, and contribute to job creation and improved grid reliability. As investment in carbon-free energy and grid infrastructure increases, these efforts can collectively help scale new technologies, drive innovation, and strengthen the overall energy ecosystem.
How Amazon is preparing for the energy needs of the future
Learn how we're supporting the transition to carbon-free energy and powering our business with sustainability in mind.
“We welcome Amazon’s continued investment in renewable energy in India. Such investments play an important role in advancing India’s clean energy ambitions, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable economic growth,” said Shri Pralhad Joshi, hon’ble union minister for new and renewable energy, education, consumer affairs, and food and public distribution. 
"They also demonstrate the growing confidence of global companies in India’s renewable energy sector and its potential to attract long-term investment, create economic opportunities, and accelerate the country’s energy transition. We look forward to continued collaboration with industry to advance India’s renewable energy goals.”
Globally, Amazon is among 
the largest corporate purchasers of carbon-free energy
, with more than 700 wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of more than 40 GW.
How Amazon is making its operations in India more sustainable
Amazon's energy investments in India are part of a broader effort to reduce the environmental footprint of its operations across electric mobility, water stewardship, and sustainable packaging.
In transportation, Amazon has deployed more than 15,000 electric vehicles across more than 500 cities and is collaborating with Tata Motors to deploy 3,000 electric trucks—the largest planned electric truck fleet by an ecommerce company in India.
For more news, visit About Amazon India
Amazon is guided by four principles: customer obsession, passion for invention, commitment to operational excellence, and long-term thinking. This is our story.
In water stewardship, Amazon 
achieved water-positive status in India in 2025
—ahead of its 2027 target—returning more than 120% of the water used across its direct operations to communities and watersheds. The company has committed more than $6 million toward water stewardship initiatives across the country. These projects are expected to replenish more than 4 billion liters of water annually and benefit local communities.
In packaging, more than 50% of customer orders in India now ship in reduced or original packaging. Amazon is also 
collaborating with the Indian Institute of Technology Roorke (IIT Roorkee)
, one of the country’s leading universities, to develop alternative packaging materials from agricultural residue, working to reduce reliance on conventional packaging materials.
